content:
Dating reality shows have always been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into this territory. While its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is nonetheless the streaming platform's first dating programme.

"The Last Person on Earth" features renowned couples therapist Esther Perel in what is described as an "innovative experiment"

Esther Perel is a famous couples therapist and New York Times bestselling author, specialising in the field of interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure of Apple TV+'s newly announced eight-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth."

According to the press release: "In this series, couples who seemingly have nothing in common will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matching experts and therapists, before embarking on a journey to the world's most romantic and remote destinations."

It sounds a lot like a reality show, but without the baggage that comes with the "reality" brand. I suspect Apple is trying to create a sense of "elevation" for dating shows, hence labelling it as a "documentary series."

The series has not yet announced a premiere date, and is expected to debut in 2027.

Incidentally, Apple also announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling novelist Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a television series. Clearly, the streaming platform hopes to break out of its current core genres of sci-fi, comedy and thriller, and venture into new territory.

Apple TV+ costs US$12.99 per month, and discounts are also available through the Apple One bundle service.
